summary.text: Joann Ariola represents the 32nd District on the New York City Council, which includes Howard Beach, Ozone Park, Woodhaven, Broad Channel and the Rockaway Peninsula in Queens.
Her Council biography says she won a Republican primary on June 22, 2021, was elected that November, and began a second term after an unchallenged election in 2023.

paragraphs.text: Ariola is a lifelong resident of the 32nd District, born in Ozone Park and raised in Howard Beach, according to her Council biography.
She attended P.S. 63, P.S. 207, Our Lady of Grace Catholic School, Stella Maris High School and Adelphi Business School.

The biography describes her as a longtime Queens civic leader and says she sponsored Int. 1001, which holds landlords accountable for knowingly renting properties to individuals selling unlicensed marijuana products.
It says she introduced Reso 5 in early 2024 calling on the city to return workers who were removed for not complying with COVID-19 vaccine requirements.
It credits her with creating the Office of Marine Debris and Removal to clean waterways around Jamaica Bay.
